name: Tufts University
character: The main campus sits on Walnut Hill with Uphill and Downhill sections, featuring a wrought-iron fence, 19th-century Italianate and modern buildings, and Boston skyline views.

landmarks.name: Walnut Hill
landmarks.quote: Tufts' main campus is located on Walnut Hill in Medford and Somerville
landmarks.look: A prominent hill overlooking the Boston skyline.

landmarks.name: Ballou Hall
landmarks.quote: Ballou Hall was constructed from 1852 to 1854 and was designed in the Italianate style

landmarks.name: Tisch Library
landmarks.quote: particularly the patio on the Tisch Library roof.
landmarks.look: A library building with a rooftop patio.

landmarks.name: academic quad
landmarks.quote: The academic quad contains the earliest buildings
landmarks.look: A grassy quad surrounded by historic 19th-century buildings and a wrought-iron fence.

landmarks.name: residential "Rez" quad
landmarks.quote: comprises the academic and the residential "Rez" quad (built on the former reservoir site)
landmarks.look: A modern residential quad enclosed by a wrought-iron fence.

landmarks.name: Carmichael Hall
landmarks.quote: The most notable building is Carmichael Hall (1954), designed by Arland A. Dirlam.

landmarks.name: Packard Hall
landmarks.quote: Other notable buildings include: Packard Hall (1856), East Hall (1860), West Hall (1871)

landmarks.name: Eaton Hall
landmarks.quote: Goddard Hall (1883), Barnum Hall (1884), and Eaton Hall (1908).
